title: Apple Leaks Low-Cost iPhone 18 Specs: Affordable Features Unveiled by 9to5Mac
body:
Apple is reportedly set to broaden its iPhone lineup next spring with the addition of a budget‑friendly “iPhone 18e,” joining the flagship iPhone 18 and the newly announced iPhone Air 2. The leak, which surfaced earlier this week, suggests the 18e will retain many of the core features that have defined Apple’s premium devices while offering a more accessible price point, potentially reshaping the company’s strategy in the highly competitive mid‑range market.

According to the information obtained, the iPhone 18e will be powered by the same A18 Bionic chip that underpins the iPhone 18, but it will likely ship with a modest 4GB of RAM instead of the 6GB found in its higher‑end sibling. Apple appears to be pairing the chip with a 6.1‑inch OLED display that maintains the 120‑Hz ProMotion refresh rate, albeit with a slightly lower peak brightness and a reduced resolution to keep costs down. The device is expected to feature a dual‑camera system— a 48‑megapixel primary sensor and a 12‑megapixel ultrawide lens—mirroring the hardware found on the iPhone 14 Pro models, but without the telephoto lens and LiDAR scanner that differentiate the premium offerings.

Design-wise, the iPhone 18e seems poised to adopt the flat‑edge chassis introduced with the iPhone 15 series, using an aluminum frame rather than the stainless‑steel build of the iPhone 18. The rear panel will likely retain the familiar matte glass finish, while the front will sport a reduced notch size compared to the flagship, preserving most of the screen real estate. Apple is also expected to continue its commitment to environmental sustainability by incorporating recycled aluminum and rare‑earth elements, a move that aligns with the company’s broader green initiatives.

Pricing will be the most compelling aspect of the 18e. Analysts project a launch price in the US around $599, positioning it well below the iPhone 18’s anticipated $999 tag and even undercutting the current iPhone SE, which starts at $429 but lacks many of the newer display and camera technologies. By offering a device that bridges the gap between the entry‑level SE and the premium lineup, Apple could capture price‑sensitive consumers who have historically migrated to Android alternatives such as Samsung’s Galaxy A series or Google’s Pixel “a” models.

The introduction of a low‑cost iPhone at this juncture reflects Apple’s response to shifting market dynamics. While the company’s premium devices continue to generate high margins, growth in mature markets like the United States and Europe has slowed, prompting a pivot toward volume‑driven segments. Moreover, the global smartphone market is projected to see a modest contraction in 2025, with emerging economies demanding affordable yet capable devices. By expanding its ecosystem with a competitively priced 18e, Apple may bolster its services revenue—particularly iCloud, Apple Music, and the App Store—by bringing more users into its hardware fold.

If the leak proves accurate, the iPhone 18e could also serve as a testing ground for future hardware tricks. Apple might experiment with modular accessories, refined AI‑driven photography, or even a more aggressive rollout of satellite connectivity at a lower price point. Such innovations would not only differentiate the 18e from other budget smartphones but also set the stage for incremental upgrades across the entire product family.

Looking ahead, the success of the iPhone 18e will hinge on how well Apple balances cost reduction with the brand’s reputation for quality and performance. Should the device deliver a compelling mix of high‑end internals, a polished design, and a price that resonates with cost‑conscious buyers, it could reinvigorate Apple’s market share in the mid‑range segment and reinforce the company’s ecosystem dominance. The upcoming spring launch will therefore be a pivotal moment, offering a clear signal of Apple’s strategic direction as it navigates an increasingly price‑sensitive global smartphone landscape.
